Welcome to Sarisbury C of E Junior School
I am extremely proud to be the Headteacher at Sarisbury C of E Junior School and lead the amazing staff and children within our school community. Our vision is to provide an educational environment in which everyone is empowered to reach their true potential.
As a Church school, our values of Compassion, Courage and Creativity permeate through everything we do and through our daily Collective Worship we explore our values through moments of reflection and celebration.
We provide an engaging curriculum which includes a wide range of opportunities to enable pupils to thrive, including themed days, school trips and the chance to represent the school in many sporting and musical events. This includes learning to play instruments with ‘Beyond the Beat’ and represent the school within an orchestra.
Please come and visit our school and let our own Year 6 Team Captains provide a personalised guided tour of the school they love being part of.

pageCache.pageTitle: Educational Visits | Sarisbury C of E Junior School
pageCache.text:
Educational Visits
At Sarisbury C of E Junior School, we believe that children learn from hands-on experiences and therefore we organise a range of educational visits in every year group. These experiences often help hook children into a topic and often are used to support the work that children complete back at school.
Alongside regular trips, during Year 4, Year 5 and Year 6, children have the opportunity to go on a residential visit. Payments for our educational visits can be made via your Scopay account which can be accessed below:
A summary of the visits each year group has had over the years can be found below:
Year 3
Sarisbury Green/Winchester
In the Autumn Term, we compare Sarisbury Green with Winchester, thinking about their geographical features and how they differ.
To reinforce our learning about our History topic – ‘Stone Age to the Iron Age’ – we visit Butser Ancient Farm, in the Spring term, to find out more about how they lived and become historians for the day.
Swanwick Lakes Nature Reserve
During the Summer term, we visit Swanwick Lakes to learn more about how soil is made and about different types of rocks to reinforce our Science knowledge.
Year 4
The Sustainability Centre
To support their work on the Anglo-Saxons, Year 4 visit The Sustainability Centre in the Autumn term.
The main topic in the Spring term is all about the Titanic. Children visit the Sea City museum to find out more about what we know happened and what was learnt following the disaster.
In the Summer term, Year 4 embed their understanding of habitats and biomes. They take a nature walk around Holly Hill, taking in the natural beauty of our local woodland and participating in Geography field work skills.
Year 5
As part of our Geography learning, we go on a river trip and look at all the different features of our local river – The Hamble – from the source to the mouth.
RESIDENTIAL – Avon Tyrrell
For our first residential trip, we spend three days (two nights) away at the Avon Tyrrell Study Centre in the New Forest. We take part in a variety of challenging tasks, pushing us out of our comfort zone and building relationships with others in the year group.
During the Summer term as part of their Tudors History topic, Year 5 visit the Mary Rose Museum to learn about the significance of the Mary Rose and the legacy that it left.
Year 6
Warner Bros Studios (Harry Potter World)
Our key topic in the Autumn term is Harry Potter. During the trip, we are able to see how the creators of the films took the details from the books and put them onto the screen. This also acts as a great stimulus for our writing about the shops in Diagon Alley in our English lessons.
RESIDENTIAL – Stone Farm Study Centre
As a celebration after the completion of SATs tests, in the Summer Term, we spend some time away at the Stone Farm Study Centre in Devon. We look after the different animals as well as having fun day trips out such as visiting and learning about local history at Morwellham Quay and during a walk on Dartmoor. Furthermore, on the way home, children have the great opportunity to search for their very own fossils on Charmouth beach, following in the footsteps of Mary Anning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sports News | Sarisbury C of E Junior School
pageCache.text:
Sports News
At Sarisbury C of E Junior School, children have the opportunity to represent the school in many ways whether that be competing for their colour team during the annual SJS School Games or as a member of our individual sports teams or events.
During children’s time at Sarisbury CE Junior School, children have many different opportunities to participate in a range of sporting competitions and events. Whether it be as a member of one of many school football teams, our swimming squad, cricket team, netball squad, cross-country running squad and many more, there is lots of opportunities.
Furthermore, annually, children have the great opportunity to compete alongside their peers and members of their colour teams during our sports afternoons. They compete to be the winning colour team for the year.
You can find some highlights from sporting matches, competitions and events this year below:
Latest News
Girls’ Hampshire Plate Semi-Final
(Wednesday 30th April)
It is a fantastic achievement to play in a semi-final and our girls loved the opportunity. On Wednesday 30th April, our Upper School Girls’ team played Ports Down in the semi-final of the Hampshire Plate. It was a tough game with the heat and a very defensive opposition. Our girls controlled the play for much of the game, showing great creativity in their passing – Evelyn ran the show through the middle and spread the ball wide to Thea, Ivy, Matilda and Indie brilliantly. It felt like only a matter of time before we would score however shortly before half-time, Ports Down managed to break through and slot the ball into our goal.
After a half-time breather and reset, our girls were back to dominating the game – everyone had to dig deep and raise their game: pressing the opposition more quickly, being more decisive in their passing and battling non-stop. Elsa, Darcie and Eliza kept the opposition away from our goal superbly. We were definitely getting closer to the equaliser but we just couldn’t get clear opportunities in Ports Down’s box. Early in the 2nd half, Indie took possession of the ball in the opposition’s half and took an early short, which flew low past their goalie – we were back in it. From that moment, we were again on top but time ran away from us. Full-time and the score was 1:1.
So to extra-time, which was flew by. Unfortunately, we just couldn’t find a way through the stoic defence of Ports Down, however hard we tried and however much was passed the ball across the pitch with ease. After extra-time the score was still 1:1. So to penalties.
This is where all our girls showed incredible courage and bravery – Amelia stood strong in goal and saved a few. Our penalty takers picked their spot and shot with great power – Evelyn scored superbly but unfortunately Ports Down’s keeper managed to save a few too. After 5 penalties for each team, Ports Down had won 2:1.
I am so proud of our girls, they played really well and showed such great determination to keep going, battling to the end and demonstrating amazing courage to step up for a penalty. I couldn’t have asked any more of you all. Well done to all our girls, it has been such a successful year for girls football reaching the final of the League Cup and semi-final of the Hampshire Plate.
Champions’ League
In our first Champions League match – aiming to retain our trophy – we played Locks Heath Juniors. We blew them away with our intense pressing and superb passing. We were certainly in control of all match with little challenge. Our Yellows beat their A team 2:0 with very quick goals in the first half. Our Reds beat their B team 8:0 – using their great pace and passing to create chance after chance. There were some superb team goals in this match – I think Freddie and Frankie had their own goal-scoring competition as they got a hat-trick each. Our Reds then played a close game against Locks Heaths A team which ended in a 0:0 draw – we just couldn’t get that clear chance to score. Finally, our Yellows played their B team and won 4:1 – it was tough to begin with as they had been waiting around for a while after playing the first match. All in all, getting 10 points out of a possible 12 is a great result so well done to all those who played. Next week we play Ranvilles Junior.
Under 11s’ Hampshire Cup Quarter Final
On Wednesday, our Upper School footballers played in the Quarter-Final of the Hampshire Cup against Wellstead from Hedge End. From the off, Sarisbury blew them away. Within about a minute, Rupert had scored to give us a fantastic start. Throughout the first half, it was wave after wave of superb attacking from our team. Wellstead barely had a chance to get near our goal. Noah had a fairly relaxed game, which was a surprise for a Quarter-Final. Our team played their best football of the season so far with outstanding passing and movement to enable us to get into goal-scoring opportunities with ease. By half-time, we were 6:0 up.
The second half continued in the same fashion as the first – resolute defending to keep Wellstead attackers away from our goal; superb passing (including switch balls to free wingers who were clean through on goal); and excellent pressing to retrieve the ball, never giving Wellstead any time. In the second half, we scored 3 more goals and Wellstead did manage to get one. The final score was 9:1 to Sarisbury – quite a thrashing for this stage of the competition. Ollie scored 4 goals, Ben got 3 and Louis and Rupert each scored one. It was truly an outstanding performance from our team – their dedication and endless drive is wonderful to see. Well done guys. Now on to the Semi-Final.
🏆 School Games’ Results 2024 🏆
This year saw our colour teams, once again, competing against each other over two great afternoons, full of great sportsmanship, resilience and teamwork. Alongside the competitive races, it was lovely to see children wanting to achieve their own personal bests with the range of playground events: jumping, shuttle runs and throwing events. Pupil Premium Support
At Sarisbury C of E Junior School, we support children who are entitled to Pupil Premium funding in many different ways. You can find some of these details below:
What is the Pupil Premium?
The pupil premium is a Government initiative that provides additional money for pupils entitled to free school meals. The premium is provided to support these pupils in their learning in order to reach their potential. The Government does not specify how schools should use this money, but are clear that schools will need to employ strategies and resources that they know will support pupils towards at least good attainment and progress.
In the financial year April 2021 to March 2022, the school received £64,995 in pupil premium funding.
In the financial year April 2020 to March 2021, the school received £65,245 in pupil premium funding.
In the financial year April 2019 to March 2020, the school received £61,000 in pupil premium funding.
How is the Pupil Premium being used at Sarisbury?
We have used our Pupil Premium allocation to fund the following:
support for extra-curricular activities and residential visits
How is the impact of the Pupil Premium evaluated?
The school evaluates the impact of this additional support alongside our regular assessment cycle. Evaluation focuses on academic gains and personal development learning; including how pupils’ self-confidence has improved as a consequence of intervention. Recommendations for the following term are then agreed.
What has the impact been so far?
To date, the Pupil Premium has contributed to:
increased confidence of pupils in their learning

Our Vision
Our School Vision is founded upon the words in Luke 2:40: And the child grew and became strong; he was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was on him.
With this as our foundation we aim to create a compassionate community of life-long learners (increasing in wisdom) empowered with the courage (to grow and become strong) to embrace creativity and achieve their potential regardless of background or ability (the grace of God was upon him).
Our core Christian values at Sarisbury Church of England Junior School are Courage, Compassion and Creativity. We strive to hold these values in our hearts and live them in our lives. They are at the very core of everything we do in school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Remote Learning | Sarisbury C of E Junior School
pageCache.text:
Remote Learning
At Sarisbury C of E Junior School, we know that there are sometimes children that need to access learning from home. All children have access to a wide variety of online learning platforms and games. Completion of tasks in Home Learning is celebrated in school.
Seesaw
Children’s home learning is set each week using the online platform, Seesaw. We use this to assign spellings as well as other home learning projects/information.
Mathletics
Mathletics is set weekly as home learning and is linked to the learning in class. Additionally, children can choose to practise further skills.
Each child is expected to gain 1000 points each week to achieve a Bronze Certificate.
Times Table Rockstars
Times Tables Rockstars is a maths program that boosts children’s fluency in the recall of multiplication facts. It is a safe, fun interactive program that allows children to collect points and create avatars as well as challenge one another.
Linguascope
Linguascope provides interactive resources and materials for students to practise their French and Spanish learning; in addition, they can also learn other languages if they want too!
Sora
Sora is a student’s reading app from Hampshire Library Service.
Children can borrow and enjoy e-books/audio books and other reading materials from this app.

Attendance & Medicines
At Sarisbury C of E Junior School, we see the importance of children’s attendance and the impact that it can have on children socially as well as academically. You can find more information about our procedures below.
At Sarisbury C of E Junior School we are committed to meeting our obligation with regards to school attendance through our whole-school culture and ethos that values good attendance, including:
We will also promote and support punctuality in attending lessons.
As a school, the Department of Education expects us to monitor attendance carefully and contact parents/carers of pupils whose attendance is dropping below 95%. We understand that some absences are unavoidable but we have a duty to follow up and discuss any issues.
If your child’s attendance drops below 90% they are considered to be at risk of underachievement. If this happens you will be receiving a letter from the school informing you and an invitation to discuss any issues with us. The aim of this is to see how we can support your child to return to good attendance.

Pupils are expected to:
Attend school every day on time.
Attending a medical or dental appointment will be counted as authorised as long as the pupil’s parent/carer notifies the school by e-mail on [email protected] or call on (01489) 573000 in advance of the appointment.
However, we encourage parents/carers to make medical and dental appointments out of school hours where possible. Where this is not possible, the pupil should be out of school for the minimum amount of time necessary.
The school or local authority can fine parents/carers for the unauthorised absence of their child from school, where the child is of compulsory school age.
Sarisbury C of E Juniors School, along with Hampshire County Council, will use the full range of legal measures to secure good attendance. Legal measures will only be considered when there is unauthorised absence and:
• Support from any agency to improve the attendance has been unsuccessful;
• The child has 10 or more sessions of unauthorised absence and parents are complicit in the child’s absence;
• A Penalty Notice has previously been issued but further unauthorised absences continue to happen.
Where a child has unauthorised absence, the school must enforce Hampshire’ s Code of Conduct for issuing Penalty Notices or follow its guidance on other Legal Measures for Non-Attendance.
The Code of Conduct is a statutory document that ensures that powers for legal sanctions are applied consistently and fairly across all schools and their families within the authority. A copy is available from https://www.hants.gov.uk/educationandlearning/behaviour-attendance-parents#step-7
Please see our Attendance Policy for more information.

pageCache.text:
Inclusion & SEND
Our vision for pupils with SEND is to provide high quality teaching that allows children to achieve strong outcomes and strive for success. Through our core Christian values of compassion, courage and creativity, we ensure equality of education and opportunity for all pupils. Teachers develop a good understanding of pupil’s strengths and barriers to learning and through this knowledge they adapt teaching and learning to ensure that our rich and relevant curriculum is inclusive for all learners.
SEND Provision at SJS
At SJS, our Special Education Needs Coordinator (SENCo) is Rebecca Paddock. For any queries with regards to SEN provision, she can be contacted via the school admin team.
Please follow the links below for further information and partnership websites:
Key Documents
Helpful Websites:
There are lots of websites that can give your further support and guidance with a range of learning needs.
Social, Emotional & Mental Health
Cognition & Learning
Please find below a range of information about how children with additional learning needs are supported during their time at Sarisbury C of E Junior School:
At Sarisbury CE Junior School children are identified as having Special Educational Needs or a Disability through a variety of ways these include:– Information received from Infant Schools/previous school– Concerns raised by teacher or by a parent– The child performing significantly below age related expectations, when measured against the national curriculum key performance indicators.– Results from in-school screening or assessments– A health diagnosis from a paediatrician or consultant– Liaison with external agencies i.e physical/auditory
If you have any concern about your child’s progress please come and speak to us. As a School, we pride ourselves on an open, honest and positive relationship with parents and we ask that you initially contact your child’s class teacher who will pass on the information and concerns to the school’s Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENCo): Mrs Rebecca Paddock. We will listen and discuss your concerns with you and may carry out informal and formal assessments where necessary to help us understand more about where your child may have barriers to their learning progress. Working in partnership with you the school will assist in organising support from external agencies where appropriate.
The schools SENCo oversees all support and progress of the children who require support that may be different from or additional to the broad range of support offered through teaching and learning in classrooms. The class teacher is responsible for the progress of all children in their class and they work in consultation with the SENCo when writing Personal learning plans which identify children’s strengths, progress and interventions where appropriate, for all pupils who are identified as having a special educational need. The Special Needs Code of Practice sets out clear guidelines and support when identifying pupils with special educational needs.Special Educational Needs provision can be considered under these four broad areas:– Communication and Interaction– Cognition and Learning– Social, Mental and Emotional Health– Sensory and/or PhysicalThe SENCo will liaise with class teachers; Learning Support Assistants (LSAs); parents and professionals working with your child. The SENCo reports to Governors about the progress and provision offered to pupils with special educational needs and shares new information relating to the area of SEND. All members of staff respect confidentiality and safeguarding concerns in school.
Class teachers are responsible for planning and teaching all children in their class ensuring they all have access to high quality inclusive teaching so that all pupils make progress including those with Special Educational Needs. Class teachers will ensure children’s needs are supported fully throughout the curriculum. Under the direction of the class teacher a Learning Support Assistant (LSA) may work with your child either individually or as part of a group to assist them in their learning or to implement a specific targeted intervention programmes.
The SENCo oversees the range of support, provision and interventions for all pupils who have additional learning needs to ensure that they are achieving. The SENCo will also support teachers in planning for and teaching pupils with Special Educational needs.
A Personal learning plan is written and reviewed up to three times a year for all pupils; these identify children’s strengths, progress and specific targets or intervention for areas of need. This may also outline class based support being used to ensure children maintain progress.
These interventions and support will be recorded on a provision map and their effectiveness is reviewed regularly by the SENCo. Pupils’ progress is reviewed at least termly and information from these meetings highlights how further support could be planned.
Occasionally a pupil may need more expert support from an outside agency such as the Educational Psychologist, Speech and Language Therapist etc. A referral will be made, with your consent and forwarded to the most appropriate agency. After a series of assessments, a programme of support is usually provided to the school and parents/carers.
If a child requires a significant amount of additional support to allow them to access the curriculum as a school we may apply for an Education, Health and Care plan to support your child.
In order to do this your child would need to meet the criteria set out in the Special Educational Needs code of practice which would be discussed with the advice and guidance of the school’s Educational Psychologist. The school would then make an application to the local authority via the EHCP Hub (an online application platform) so that learning plan required to support your child can be formal recognised in a statutory document – the Educational, Health and Care Plan. Should your child be given an Educational Health and Care plan that would support their needs until the age of 25 years. These EHCPs are reviewed annually to ensure that targets are met and relevant to support your child on their educational journey.
The class teacher will share Personal learning plans with you at least termly and if needed the SENCo and class teacher will meet with you more regularly to discuss and review individual targets and progress. Liaison with support assistants takes place informally at convenient times. Meetings with parents and professionals may be held at any time as needed. The SENCo hold termly parents evening meeting for any parents of children who have additional needs if required.
Our nominated SEND governor is Mrs Marisa Lamb. The SENCo meets with the governor responsible for SEND regularly and produces a report which outlines all areas of SEND. The SEND Governor shares updates on SEND regularly at governor meetings.
Each term the governors receive a report that informs them about the progress of children with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities; this report does not refer to individual children and confidentiality is maintained. The governors maintain an overview of the allocation of resources ensuring there is effective provision for all pupils with additional learning needs.
When planning the curriculum teachers need to consider an appropriate match of task to all children’s strengths and confidences.
Wave 1 – Inclusive quality-first teaching for all:
Receiving targeted teaching in class either with teacher or with an LSA (who is guided by the teacher). The activity may be adapted depending upon need.
Wave 2 – Additional targeted intervention in a small group:
Teacher or LSA led group focusing on a key skill usually a couple of times a week.
Wave 3 – Additional targeted intervention in a small group:
Some pupils require 1-1 support for approximately an hour a week accessing a recognised intervention programme. This is usually delivered by an LSA.
Appropriate match maybe through the type of activity or the resources required by the child to complete the task. If applicable, specialist equipment will be provided for a pupil. LSAs can be allocated to work with the pupil in a 1-1 or in a small focus group to target more specific curriculum needs.
When a pupil has been identified with Special Education Needs or a Disability their work will be pitched appropriately to allow them to achieve the learning objectives which will enable them to access the curriculum.
We offer an open-door policy where you are welcome to make an appointment to meet with either the class teacher or SENCo and discuss how your child is getting on. We can offer advice and practical ways that you can use to support your child at home.
The school holds parents’ evenings twice a year where teachers will share with parents and the child their progress using the schools ‘steps to success’, which outlines the progress the child has made; and where they are working in relation to age related expectations for their year group, as well as targets for their learning. Parents also receive an annual report written by the class teacher. If a child on the SEND register has received support for an intervention from an LSA throughout the year, parents will also receive a summary report on their progress.
We track children’s progress in learning (from entry at Yr3 through to YR6) against National age-related expectations, using: teacher assessment; statutory tests in Yr6 and assessments of reading and spelling ages.
Through effective communication between yourselves, teachers, across our learning support team and the SENCo we aim to ensure a continuity of care within the year and at points of transition.
The SEND budget is allocated each financial year, and through the governing body SEND finances are monitored and reviewed regularly. The money is used to provide additional support or resources dependent upon need. Resources may include deployment of staff depending on individual circumstances.
The SENCo constantly audits the provision and resources available to support SEND and produces an SEND action plan annually. Some of the budget may be used to fulfil targets on the action plan.
Pupils’ progress is actively tracked and reviewed termly and the SENCo discusses the progress of children with Special Educational Needs with each class teacher regularly. These discussions review a child’s needs; what level of support would be appropriate and the type of intervention the child will receive. This information is shared with you on the Personal learning plan
Different children will require different levels of support to accelerate progress and bridge the gap to achieve age related expectations.
When pupils have to sit end of key stage Statutory Assessments, careful planning is undertaken by the Year 6 team to ensure that all pupils are prepared for the tests and they follow the national guidelines that outlines the additional support that can be put in place for pupils with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities. This may involve the use of a reader, scribe or the allocation of extra time.
We work in partnership with parents to support each child’s well-being, learning needs, progress and aspirations. Along with our open-door policy parents are encouraged to contribute to their child’s education through:
-discussions with the class teacher
– attending parents’ evening
-discussions with the SENCo or external agencies
-supporting Individual learning plan targets at home.
Parents can comment on the day-to –day running of the school through an annual questionnaire and a parental forum.
As a caring school, we believe that children’s self-esteem and well-being is paramount in their education.
The class teacher has overall responsibility for the pastoral, medical and social care of each child in their class, therefore this would be the parents’ first point of contact. If further support is required the class teacher liaises with the SENCo for further support and advice. Where appropriate the school works closely alongside outside agencies such as Health and Social Services or the Behaviour Support Team.
The school has a two highly experienced and well-trained ELSA (Emotional Literacy Support Assistant) and Family link worker who works under the direction of the SENCo with vulnerable children. The emotional support they receive is dependent upon need, and its impact on the child’s well-being is reviewed regularly.
Staff receive training for certain medical conditions when required and if a child has a medical condition a care plan is compiled with support from the school nurse or other health professionals, this is shared with all staff who work with the pupil. The school produces a directory of all children with medical conditions and health care recommendations for all staff. This directory is updated regularly to ensure continuity of care.
At all times, there will be a qualified first aider on site and staff receive emergency first aid training at regular intervals.
Parents need to contact the school office if Health Professionals recommend medication to be taken during the school day as it can only be administered after a medical form has been signed and received by the school office. On a day to day basis the Admin Staff generally oversee the administration of any medicines.
For further information please refer to our First Aid and Drugs Policy.
As a school, we have a very positive approach to all types of behaviour with a clear reward system that is followed by all staff and pupils.
If a child presents challenging behaviours an Individual Behaviour Management Plan (IBMP) is written alongside the child and parents to identify the specific issues, put relevant support in place and set targets. pageCache.text:
Music
Please find below a summary of what children are taught during Music lessons at Sarisbury C of E Junior School as well as other helpful documents.
Music is life itself. What would this world be without good music?”
– Louis Armstrong
Our KS2 Music curriculum at Sarisbury C of E Junior School empowers children to develop a love for Music and to establish Music as a powerful tool that can inspire, excite and calm. Our curriculum is guided by our core Christian values to ensure our pupils gain the confidence to become creative musicians, courageous performers and compassionate listeners.
Children’s musical journey at SJS begins in Years 3 and 4, where they are given the opportunity to access and make progress on a musical instrument through our ‘Listen 2 Me” and “Beyond the Beat” programmes run by Hampshire Music Service.
In Year 5 and Year 6, children build on their musical skills and knowledge as composers and performers through class-based music opportunities linked closely to topic themes.
Club activities enrich the school’s music provision where children have the opportunity to learn and perform in an excellent school choir and a variety of music ensembles.
In addition, the school offers a full range of instrumental tuition delivered through Hampshire Music Service. There is a charge for these lessons and tuition is currently offered in brass, woodwind, violin, cello, ukulele and guitar. Please contact the admin team for further information.

pageCache.text:
Home Learning
At Sarisbury C of E Junior School, we see home learning as a important bridge between the work completed at school. You can find more details about how we structure Home Learning below:
Generally, home learning involves practising spellings, reading for 20 minutes daily and an additional task relating to the work completed within school.
In particular, we believe that reading is an essential component of what can be completed at home. This can also involve developing a love of reading by sharing a book together or by taking it in turns to read. Fundamentally, reading for 20 minutes a day has a big impact on pupils’ attainment (Nagy and Herman, 1987):
– If a child reads for 20 minutes a day, children will read for 3,600 minutes per school year and read 1,800,000 words per school year.
– If a child reads for 5 minutes a day, children will read for 900 minutes per school year and read 282,000 words per school year.
– If a child reads for 1 minute a day, children will read for 180 minutes per school year and read 8,000 words per school year.
Alongside this, we give children access to lots of online platforms that can benefit children in a range of different learning areas. Details of this can be found on our Remote Learning page:
